title: This Seabird Flew Almost 40,000 Miles in One Year, Tracked by Tiny Tags

scenes.text: This seabird flew almost forty thousand miles in one year.
It's the sooty shearwater, and scientists tracked it with tiny tags.
It breeds near New Zealand and Chile, then flies all the way to the north Pacific.
Then it flies back south. A full loop around the entire ocean.
It crosses the equator twice, chasing food and endless summer.
That's the longest animal migration ever tracked with electronics. Almost forty thousand miles.

description:
This seabird flew almost forty thousand miles in one year.
Sooty shearwaters were tracked with tiny tags on a loop around the whole Pacific, crossing the equator twice.
How far would you fly for endless summer?
first_comment: Only the Arctic tern might rival it, but nobody had tracked a tern when this study came out. Which bird should we track next?
